title: The stamp that changed communication
text: It was Rowland Hill {{1}} transformed the British post in 1840. Before his reform, postage {{2}} calculated by distance and paid by the recipient, {{3}} meant that many poor families simply refused deliveries, forcing senders {{4}} encode secret messages on the envelope so that the letter could be read and thrown away unpaid. In {{5}} end, Hill's solution was beautifully simple: charge {{6}} flat penny, paid in advance, whatever the distance travelled. The Penny Black, {{7}} bore the young Queen's profile, went on sale that May, and within a year the number of letters had more than doubled. {{8}} is hard now to imagine the revolution this tiny printed scrap began: communication between ordinary people, once a luxury, had become a cheap everyday habit.

gaps.hint: relative: it was Rowland Hill ___ transformed
gaps.explanation: Cleft sentence about a person: only 'who' fits after the name.
Past passive with an uncountable singular subject: was calculated.
Sentential relative after the comma; 'that' is impossible here.
'Force someone to do' — the infinitive follows the object.
'In the end' is the fixed phrase for the outcome.
First mention of a singular countable noun takes 'a'.

gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative about a thing after the comma.

gaps.explanation: 'It is hard to imagine' — the dummy subject before the infinitive.
